newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's BNA bank to recover $980 mln debt.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's BNA bank to recover $980 mln debt.

text.p: Tunisia's Banque Nationale Agricole BNA is to recover a 980 million dinars ($980 million) bad debt owed to it by cereals and olive oil state bodies.

The 1997 Appropriations Law (finance law) received on Thursday includes a decision by which the state guarantees the repurchase by the Central Bank of the 900 million dinars debt owed to BNA by Office des Cereales and Office National de l'Huile as of December 31, 1996.

Budget documents showed that the rescheduled debt, which represents nearly ten fold BNA's capital of 100 million dinars, will be paid by the government to the Central Bank over 12 years and without interest.
Officials said the repurchase was aimed at helping BNA, a state-controlled bank, consolidate its accounts to conform with banking safety rules.
BNA's net profits for the first half of 1996 amounted to 8.766 million dinars. They were 14.693 million dinars for the whole year 1995.
BNA's shares were last priced 33.8 dinars at the Tunis Stock Exchange. ($=one dinar)
